observation.visible_scene: Extreme close-up of a glossy pink semi-solid mass resting on a bed of white granular particles. The upper pink surface has scattered clear flaky crystals and a wet sheen, while its lower boundary meets the granules.
visible_changes: The pink mass slowly deforms in place; its lower contour becomes smoother and less sharply defined against the granular bed.
The surface becomes wetter and glossier, and the clear flaky crystals on it become less distinct or fewer over time.
A translucent pink liquid layer develops at the base of the mass, first as small patches near the right side and later as a broader film spreading into the granules.
The white granules adjacent to the pink mass become darker and partly obscured by liquid, while the bulk granular bed remains largely stationary.
The mass does not visibly translate across the frame; the main visible change is local spreading, surface wetting, and liquid accumulation around its lower edge.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the liquid to form or whether an external liquid was added.
The exact materials of the pink mass, crystals, and granules.
Whether the spreading/wetting process began before this excerpt or continues after it.
uncertain_details: Small apparent shifts of the pink/liquid boundary may include slight camera framing changes; background evidence is insufficient to separate them from physical deformation.
Whether the crystals dissolve, are displaced, or are simply covered by the liquid is not directly observable.
